name: Las Vegas
title: Holidays in Las Vegas
intro: The neon city in the Nevada desert, with themed mega-resorts, big shows and pools, and the Grand Canyon and Red Rock Canyon within reach. Here's what Las Vegas is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The Las Vegas Strip at night, with the Bellagio fountains and hotel lights
facts_note: Most hotels add a daily resort fee on top of the room rate. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: March, April, October and November are the best months, warm and sunny without the extreme summer heat. June to August often tops 40°C, though pools and air conditioning help. Winter is cool and dry, and good value outside big holiday weekends.

things.name: The Strip
things.blurb: Walk past the Bellagio fountains, a mini Eiffel Tower and Venice canals inside the Venetian.

things.name: Shows
things.blurb: Cirque du Soleil, magic and big-name residencies.

things.name: Sphere
things.blurb: A giant LED-covered globe with immersive films and concerts inside.

things.name: Fremont Street
things.blurb: Old Vegas downtown, under a canopy of light shows.

things.name: Red Rock Canyon
things.blurb: Red sandstone cliffs and hiking trails, 30 minutes from the Strip.

things.name: Grand Canyon
things.blurb: The West Rim and Skywalk is about 2.5 hours away. The South Rim is a longer trip.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Las Vegas?
faqs.answer: Three or four days covers the Strip, a show and a day trip. Add more if you plan to road trip to the national parks.

faqs.question: Is Las Vegas good for families?
faqs.answer: More than you'd think: pools, shows, aquariums and roller coasters, though children can't go on casino floors.

faqs.question: Can you visit the Grand Canyon from Las Vegas?
faqs.answer: Yes. The West Rim is about 2.5 hours by road. The South Rim is about 4.5 hours, so it's better with an overnight stay.

faqs.question: When is Las Vegas cheapest?
faqs.answer: Midweek, outside big conventions and holidays. Weekend room rates can be several times higher.
